evaluations.label: A
errors: Action items list only two items (room separation, asking Maggie and Pierrette); the transcript also has Andre checking whether four places fit in the three-person room and asking about placing Gisella with the school's other admin staff, and everyone preparing preferences or a sketch.
Says Martin 'warned' the reading room leaves no growth capacity; he only remarked that growth would be zero, a minor framing stretch.
Says the group 'discussed meeting' Tuesday around 2 p.m.; this was actually agreed.
strengths: Mostly faithful to the transcript, with timestamps and almost no invented content.
Correctly states that nothing was decided: the room count is fixed, assignments are open, and the lounge purpose and Gisela's placement are unresolved.
Gets the owners right for the two actions it lists (Andrei for room separation, Susan for Maggie and Pierrette).
Includes the 15 people versus 18 positions count, the 16 versus 15 arithmetic with the reading room, the smoking point and the Tuesday 2 p.m. follow-up.
weaknesses: Omits the four-places-in-a-three-person-room question, the idea of placing Gisella with the school's other admin staff, the vending machine and coffee discussion, and the equipment and other-group negotiation details.
The follow-up for participants to bring preferences and a sketch sits in a section rather than the action items.
Thin on how the lounge debate went (the 'do we need it' pushback and the mixed-use leaning).

evaluations.label: B
errors: Assigns to Andrei the task of following up with Maggie and Pierrette on their preferences; in the transcript Susan volunteered to ask them.
Lists 'Distribute documents' as an action item for Andrei; he handed out copies during the meeting, so this is not a follow-up.
Says the lounge is a 'key', 'priority' item that management recognizes; the transcript shows Susan questioning whether it is needed and the purpose is explicitly left open.
Says the team 'considers the current move a partial solution' and that 'project grouping [is] less important than proximity to meeting rooms'; neither is stated.
Says 'Others require private offices'; only Susan expressed that, and Martin said he is fine sharing.
The attributed timestamps are often inaccurate (e.g. '00:06' for the opening).
strengths: Most complete coverage: the 18 versus 15 count, zero growth, one free visitor slot, the four-in-a-three-person-room idea, the room-splitting authorization hurdle, Gisella's options, the school-admin idea, the other group, coffee and vending machines, smoking, equipment and the Tuesday afternoon follow-up.
Action items are grouped by person and include the participant task of polling colleagues and bringing a sketch or slides.
Clearly states that the meeting was for collecting constraints and not finalizing assignments.
weaknesses: Very long and repetitive; the same points (visitors, room splitting, growth) appear in several sections.
Loads nearly all follow-ups onto Andrei, which misattributes owners.
Some overstated or padded inferences presented as the group's views.

evaluations.label: C
errors: Says 'Strong support for a dedicated lounge/reading room'; Susan questioned the need and Martin wanted it to be more than a pure reading room, so 'strong' is somewhat overstated.
Next-step items have no owners, even though Susan clearly took the Maggie and Pierrette task and Andre took the room-separation question.
Describes 'Majority lean toward a mixed-use room'; only a few speakers said so and it was left an open question.
strengths: Accurate, compact and well organized by topic: space overview, seating constraints, lounge, next steps.
Captures Gisella's two options precisely (a one-person room if a professor volunteers to share, or a two-person room with a visitor slot) plus the idea of placing her with other school admin.
States that room splitting is ruled out for now but is to be confirmed, and that smoking is no longer a constraint.

Includes the 16 versus 15 slots and zero growth margin, the four-desks-in-a-three-person-room question, vending machines on floors 1 and 3 and the 5 pm cafeteria closing, and the Tuesday afternoon follow-up with the morning meeting conflict.
weaknesses: No owners on the next steps, so who does what must be inferred.
Does not say plainly that no allocation decision was reached.
Leaves out the point about asking everyone for a sketch only indirectly and omits the point that nobody will volunteer who they do not want to share with.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Action Items section says '(none)' although the meeting produced clear follow-ups (room separation, Maggie and Pierrette, Gisella, bring proposals).

Uses 'Speaker 1/2/3/4' labels that are not the speaker names, with a confusing mapping (e.g. 'Speaker 3 announced the relocation'; 'Speaker 3, Speaker 1, Speaker 2, and Speaker 4 debated'), so attributions cannot be checked or used.
Calls the 'Speaker 3 will investigate' item an unresolved question list rather than assigning owners, and gives no owner for asking Maggie and Pierrette.
'Participants discussed ... noise levels produced by administrative staff' is an unfair framing, though it traces to the discussion of Gisella.
strengths: Correct on the main facts: sixth floor, one-, two- and three-person rooms, 15 people versus about 18 slots including the reading room, furniture, equipment and the Tuesday 2 p.m. follow-up.
The Unresolved Questions list (partitions, four in a three-person room, lounge purpose, individual offices) is a useful open-issues view.
weaknesses: Generic speaker numbers make the notes hard to act on.
Misses zero growth, the one free visitor slot, the smoking point, the coffee and vending machines, the school-admin idea and the concrete options for Gisella.
No usable action items and no owners; the summary of who does what is effectively missing.
Repeats the same content in the summary and the outline.

rationale: No allocation decision was made; the useful content is the constraints, the open questions and the follow-ups (Andre checks room separation and the four-in-a-three-person-room and admin-placement questions, Susan asks Maggie and Pierrette, everyone brings preferences or a sketch, meeting Tuesday 2 pm). C is accurate, compact and covers nearly all of these, including Gisella's two options, with only the missing owners as a weakness. B is the most complete but has the wrong owner for the Maggie and Pierrette task, a few unsupported claims and heavy repetition. A is accurate but omits several open questions and action items. D uses unnamed speaker numbers, states there are no action items and misses much of the substance.
